Generate auditable sensitivity completions

Source: R/impute.R
catmech_impute.Rd

Supports one continuous target with complete predictors. Each completion uses an independent parameter and donor draw; no iterative chain is needed for this restricted setting. Categories must be observed, except that a missing category can be derived from an unflagged observed value. Predictors must be selected explicitly to avoid accidental use of identifiers or simulation truth. Include downstream outcomes when appropriate for the intended analysis. Completed data and Rubin pooling are experimental and do not establish identification, proper MI, or interval coverage.

Usage

catmech_impute(data, spec, predictors, m = 20L, seed = 1L)

Arguments

data

A data.frame. The original is stored without modification.

spec

A [catmech_spec()] or equivalent validated list.

predictors

Character vector of complete predictor column names. Use character(0) for an intercept-only model. The category, target and flag cannot be predictors. Category information restricts the donor support.

m

Number of completed datasets, at least 2.

seed

Nonnegative integer random seed. The caller's RNG is restored.

Value

A catmech_result containing original, completed, mids, audit, diagnostics, spec and manifest. mids is an analysis adapter created from the supplied completions, not evidence of mice chain convergence.

Examples

d <- simulate_catmech_lab(150, seed = 12)
d <- d[setdiff(names(d), c("lab_true", "corrupted"))]
s <- catmech_spec("lab_value", "lab_category", c("Low", "Medium", "High"),
  c(-Inf, 5.5, 7, Inf), flag = "outlier_flag", corruption_probability = 1,
  conflict_policy = "reconstruct")
fit <- catmech_impute(d, s, c("age", "sex", "inflammation", "outcome"), m = 3)
fit$diagnostics
#>   imputation requested reconstructed changed threshold_conflicts fallback_draws
#> 1          1        42            42      10                   8              0
#> 2          2        42            42      10                   8              0
#> 3          3        42            42      10                   8              0
#>   threshold_violations
#> 1                    0
#> 2                    0
#> 3                    0
